papers.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
papers.authors: Touvron, Martin, Stone, et al. (Meta AI)
papers.hint: Open-weight 7B-70B models + the RLHF chat-tuning recipe (Ghost Attention, two reward models, iterative RLHF). Pretrain on 2T tokens.

papers.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
papers.hint: 405B dense model, 15T-token pretraining, 128K context, scaling-law-driven data/compute decisions, multilingual + tool use.

papers.title: Mistral 7B
papers.hint: 7B that beats Llama-2-13B via Grouped-Query Attention + Sliding-Window Attention for cheap long context.

papers.title: Mixtral of Experts
papers.hint: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts: 8 experts, top-2 routing per token; 47B params but ~13B active. Matches GPT-3.5.

papers.title: GPT-4 Technical Report
papers.hint: Multimodal model; human-level on professional exams; predictable scaling from small runs; safety/RLHF. Few architecture details disclosed.

papers.title: Gemini 1.5: Multimodal Understanding Across Millions of Tokens
papers.hint: MoE multimodal model with up to 10M-token context; near-perfect long-context retrieval (needle-in-haystack).

papers.title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
papers.hint: 671B-param MoE (37B active), Multi-head Latent Attention, auxiliary-loss-free load balancing, FP8 training, ~$5.6M compute.

papers.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via RL
papers.hint: Reasoning emerges from pure RL (GRPO) with rule-based rewards; R1-Zero needs no SFT; long chain-of-thought 'aha moments'; distilled to small models.

papers.title: Qwen2 Technical Report
papers.hint: Dense + MoE family 0.5B-72B, strong multilingual + code/math, long context, competitive open weights.

papers.title: Gemma: Open Models Based on Gemini Research
papers.hint: 2B/7B open models distilled from Gemini tech; GeGLU, RoPE, RMSNorm; strong for their size.

papers.title: Gemma 2: Improving Open Language Models at a Practical Size
papers.hint: 2B-27B; knowledge distillation from a larger teacher into smaller students; interleaved local/global attention, logit soft-capping.

papers.title: Textbooks Are All You Need (phi-1)
papers.hint: 1.3B code model trained on a small set of 'textbook-quality' + synthetic data beats far larger models — data quality over scale.

papers.title: Phi-3 Technical Report: A Highly Capable LM Locally on Your Phone
papers.hint: 3.8B phi-3-mini rivals Mixtral/GPT-3.5 via heavily curated + synthetic data; runs on a phone.

papers.title: OLMo: Accelerating the Science of Language Models
papers.hint: Fully open LM: weights, data (Dolma), training code, logs — reproducible science, not just open weights.

papers.title: Tülu 3: Pushing Frontiers in Open Language Model Post-Training
papers.hint: Fully open post-training recipe: SFT + DPO + new RL-with-verifiable-rewards (RLVR); state-of-the-art open instruct models.

papers.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
papers.hint: Selective state-space model: input-dependent SSM parameters + hardware-aware scan; linear in sequence length, no attention, matches Transformers.

papers.title: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism
papers.hint: Exact attention, IO-aware tiling in SRAM; v2 improves work partitioning to ~2x v1, ~70% of GPU peak FLOPs. No approximation.

papers.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention
papers.hint: Tile Q,K,V into SRAM and fuse softmax so the N×N matrix is never written to HBM — exact attention, linear memory, big speedup.

papers.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models
papers.hint: Group query heads to share K/V heads — interpolates between multi-head and multi-query; shrinks the KV cache with little quality loss.

papers.title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
papers.hint: An RNN that trains in parallel like a Transformer; linear inference, constant memory; WKV linear-attention mechanism.

papers.title: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for LLMs
papers.hint: Retention mechanism with three equivalent forms (parallel/recurrent/chunkwise): train in parallel, infer O(1) per token.

papers.title: Jamba: A Hybrid Transformer-Mamba Language Model
papers.hint: Interleave Mamba (SSM) and attention layers + MoE; 256K context, high throughput, fits big context on one GPU.

papers.title: Transformers are SSMs: Mamba-2 and State Space Duality
papers.hint: Shows attention and SSMs are two views of one math (structured state-space duality); Mamba-2 is faster and easier to scale.

papers.title: The Era of 1-bit LLMs: BitNet b1.58
papers.hint: Every weight is ternary {-1,0,+1} (1.58 bits); matches FP16 quality at scale while replacing matmuls with adds.

papers.title: Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers for Near-Infinite Context
papers.hint: Distribute the sequence across devices in a ring; overlap KV communication with blockwise attention compute — context scales with device count.

papers.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
papers.hint: Keep a few initial 'attention-sink' tokens + a sliding window so a model streams indefinitely without retraining or collapsing.

papers.title: Efficient Memory Management for LLM Serving with PagedAttention
papers.hint: Page the KV cache like OS virtual memory — near-zero fragmentation, sharing across requests; ~2-4x serving throughput.

papers.title: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically Allocating Compute in Transformers
papers.hint: Let a router skip layers for easy tokens — spend compute where it matters, fixed compute budget per forward pass.

papers.title: Differential Transformer
papers.hint: Subtract two softmax attention maps to cancel attention 'noise', sharpening focus on relevant context; better long-context + retrieval.

papers.title: Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned, Natively Trainable Sparse Attention
papers.hint: Trainable sparse attention (compress + select + sliding window) aligned to GPU hardware; long-context speedups without quality loss.

papers.title: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration with Multiple Decoding Heads
papers.hint: Add extra heads that predict several future tokens at once + tree verification — speculative decoding without a separate draft model.

papers.title: YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension of Large Language Models
papers.hint: Extend RoPE context length by rescaling frequencies (NTK-by-parts) with minimal fine-tuning; cheap long-context.

papers.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs
papers.hint: Generalize chain-of-thought into a search tree of partial 'thoughts' with explicit evaluation + backtracking (BFS/DFS); solves Game-of-24.

papers.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
papers.hint: Self-supervised tool use: the model inserts API calls into text, keeps only calls that lower loss — learns calculators, search, etc.

papers.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
papers.hint: Agent reflects on failures in natural language and stores the reflection in memory to retry better — 'verbal RL', no weight updates.

papers.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with LLMs
papers.hint: Minecraft agent that writes/refines a growing skill library of code, with an automatic curriculum — lifelong learning, no gradients.

papers.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
papers.hint: 25 LLM agents in a sandbox town with memory-stream + reflection + planning — emergent believable social behavior.

papers.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
papers.hint: Model decides WHEN to retrieve and emits 'reflection tokens' to critique relevance + factual support of its own output.

papers.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
papers.hint: Build a knowledge graph + community summaries from a corpus so RAG can answer global 'sensemaking' questions, not just local lookups.

papers.title: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval
papers.hint: Recursively cluster + summarize chunks into a tree so retrieval can pull the right level of abstraction for multi-step questions.

papers.title: Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in LLMs
papers.hint: Draft answer -> generate verification questions -> answer them independently -> revise; self-checking cuts factual errors.

papers.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning (GRPO)
papers.hint: Introduces Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO): drop the value network, normalize rewards within a sampled group — the RL behind R1.

papers.title: s1: Simple Test-Time Scaling
papers.hint: 1K curated reasoning examples + 'budget forcing' (append 'Wait' to make the model think longer) gives o1-style test-time scaling cheaply.

papers.title: Self-Rewarding Language Models
papers.hint: The model acts as its own judge (LLM-as-judge) to generate preference pairs and iteratively DPO-trains on them — reward not frozen.

papers.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your LM is Secretly a Reward Model
papers.hint: Skip the reward model + RL loop: a closed-form loss optimizes preferences directly with a simple classification objective. Replaced PPO for most.

papers.title: RLAIF: Scaling RL from Human Feedback with AI Feedback
papers.hint: Replace human preference labels with an off-the-shelf LLM's labels — matches RLHF at a fraction of the labeling cost.

papers.title: ORPO: Monolithic Preference Optimization without Reference Model
papers.hint: Fold preference alignment into SFT with an odds-ratio penalty — one stage, no separate reference model or RM.

papers.title: KTO: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization
papers.hint: Align using only thumbs-up/down labels (not pairs), via a loss derived from Kahneman-Tversky prospect theory.

papers.title: Segment Anything
papers.hint: Promptable segmentation foundation model + SA-1B (1.1B masks); zero-shot segments anything from a point/box/text prompt.

papers.title: Visual Instruction Tuning (LLaVA)
papers.hint: Connect a vision encoder to an LLM with a projection layer; instruction-tune on GPT-4-generated multimodal data — open multimodal chat.

papers.title: SDXL: Improving Latent Diffusion Models for High-Resolution Synthesis
papers.hint: 3x bigger UNet, two text encoders, size/crop conditioning + a refiner — high-quality 1024px text-to-image.

papers.title: Consistency Models
papers.hint: Learn a map from any point on the diffusion trajectory straight to the clean image — one-step (or few-step) generation.

papers.title: Adding Conditional Control to Text-to-Image Diffusion Models (ControlNet)
papers.hint: Add spatial control (edges, pose, depth) to a frozen diffusion model via a trainable copy with zero-initialized convolutions.

papers.title: Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis (SD3)
papers.hint: Rectified-flow objective + a multimodal diffusion Transformer (MM-DiT) that processes text and image tokens jointly.

papers.title: Depth Anything: Unleashing the Power of Large-Scale Unlabeled Data
papers.hint: Monocular depth foundation model trained on 62M unlabeled images via a teacher-student pseudo-labeling pipeline.

papers.title: Qwen2-VL: Enhancing Vision-Language Models' Perception at Any Resolution
papers.hint: Naive dynamic resolution (any image size -> variable tokens) + multimodal rotary position embedding; strong document/video VLM.

papers.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Chinchilla)
papers.hint: For a fixed compute budget, model size and tokens should scale equally (~20 tokens/param); a 70B Chinchilla beats 280B Gopher.
